html:
The Baure are an Arawakan-speaking people of the Llanos de Moxos, the seasonally flooded plains of the Beni in northeastern Bolivia. The area around their villages holds some of the best-known earthworks of the Amazon: raised causeways, canals and zigzag fish weirs built long before Europeans arrived.

In the 1700s Jesuit missionaries founded missions among them, such as Concepción de Baures, on the model of the Jesuit reductions further south. After the Jesuits were expelled in 1767, the missions declined, and in the late 1800s the rubber boom drew many Baure into forced labour. Their language, part of the Arawakan family, now has few speakers.
